content:
We have a task: identify the compound from experimental data. We have mass spec: m/z 193.1103 (intensity 100) and isotopic pattern suggests molecular ion M+ at 193.1103. The formula we derived from isomers list: C11H15NO2 (exact mass? Let's compute: C11=132.000, H15=15.117, N=14.003, O2=31.989 => total 193.109 approx). So matches.

We have carbon NMR experimental: Deltas: 166.40, 144.78, 132.00, 130.07, 130.07, 127.80, 127.80, 52.24, 49.55, 43.55, 19.23.

We need to propose SMILES that matches formula and spectra.

We have simulated spectra for several candidate SMILES. Need to compare.

Let's list candidates we tried:

1) CCOC1=C(C=CC=N1)C(=O)C(C)C (a pyridine with ethoxy and isobutyryl?). Simulated C13 NMR: 206.40, 160.30, 137.90, 130.27, 123.57, 122.45, 62.45, 37.30, 17.90, 17.90, 14.35. Not matching experimental (166 vs 206, etc). So not.

2) COC(=O)CC1=CC=CC(=C1)CCN (anisole? Actually methyl ester). Simulated C13: 171.40, 134.46, 132.00, 128.53, 127.50, 126.60, 121.30, 51.93, 43.10, 39.90, 38.70. Experimental: 166.40, 144.78, 132.00, 130.07,130.07,127.80,127.80,52.24,49.55,43.55,19.23. Some matches: 132.00 matches, 127.8 matches 127.5/126.6, 52.24 matches 51.93, 43.55 matches 43.10, but we have extra peaks: experimental has 166.40 (likely carbonyl), 144.78 (aromatic C attached to hetero?), 130.07 double, 19.23 (methyl). Simulated has 171.40 (carbonyl), 134.46 (aromatic), 121.30 (maybe aromatic). Not perfect.

3) O=C(NC(C)(OCC))c1ccccc1 (N-acylated aniline with tert-butoxy? Actually N attached to carbonyl, N attached to C(C)(OCC) i.e., N attached to carbonyl and to a tertiary carbon bearing ethoxy). Simulated C13: 166.55, 134.27, 131.90, 128.56,128.56,127.17,127.17,111.60,62.60,19.90,15.13. Experimental: 166.40 matches 166.55, 144.78 vs 134.27 (off), 132.00 vs 131.90 (good), 130.07 vs 128.56 (close), 127.80 vs 127.17 (close), 52.24 vs 62.60 (off), 49.55 vs 111.60 (no), 43.55 vs 19.90 (no), 19.23 vs 15.13 (close). Not great.

4) CCOC1=CC=C(C(=O)NCC)C=C1 (ethyl phenylcarboxamide). Simulated? Not yet.

Let's simulate that.
